 JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.
2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
On 15-09-2024 at about 01-15 pm., the petitioner was traveling as pillion rider in a Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EV-0872 along with her husband by name Sabanna on Bangalore -Mysore service road towards Hejjala and when they reached opp Rajarajeshwara Hospital, at that time the driver of Mahindra Bolero Jeep No.KA-01-MH-9505 came from Kumbalagodu towards Kengeri service road in opposite direction in the wrong way in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's scooter, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, she was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient from 15-09-2024 to 23-09-2024.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was working as a coolie and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to permanent disability, she is not in a position to do the said work.
She has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. Respondent no.1/the insurer of Mahindra Bolero Jeep No.KA-01-MH-9505 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and Fitness certificate as on the date of accident and that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the said vehicle has been falsely implicated by the petitioner with active collusion of the owner of the motorcycle and police, in order to get the Monamma vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32640726/
2 compensation.

sentences.text: 5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 - the R.C. owner of Mahindra Bolero Jeep No.KA-01- MH-9505 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex- parte.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15-09-2024 at about 1-15 pm., on Banglore-Mysore Service Road towards Hejjala, Opposite to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, Challaghatta,
Bangalore city, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Mahindra Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.no.KA-01-MH-9505?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner got examined herself as Pw1 and two witnesses as P.W.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P24 and closed evidence from her side.
The respondent no.1 has examined its Senior Executive as Rw.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent no.1 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following;
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of Mahindra Bolero Jeep,
the P.W.1 has filed her affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 15-09-2024 at about 01-15 pm., when the petitioner was traveling as pillion rider in a Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EV-0872 along with her husband by name Sabanna on Bangalore - Mysore service road towards Hejjala and when they reached opp Rajarajeshwara Hospital, at that time the driver of Mahindra Bolero Jeep No.KA-01-MH-9505 (herein after called the offending vehicle) came Monamma vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32640726/
3 from Kumbalagodu towards Kengeri service road in opposite direction in the wrong way in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's scooter, result of which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.
In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle,

P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Spot mahazar, Seizer mahazar, Notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, IMV report,
Indemnity bonds, wound certificate and charge sheet etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the husband of petitioner by name Sabanna, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0310/2024 by Kumbalagudu Police Station for the offence punishable under section 125(a), 281 of BNS 2023.
After completion of investigation, the Investigation officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 125(b), 281 of BNS 2023.

13. The Learned counsel for respondent no.1 has argued much on the delay in lodging the complaint and submitted that the petitioner has falsely implicated the offending vehicle after due deliberation hence claim petition is not maintainable against them.

14. In the light of the objection raised by the respondent no.1 if the police documents are perused, it is true that the accident in question has occurred on 15- 09-2024 and complaint came to be lodged on 22-09- 2024 and there is delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint.

In the complaint reason for delay has been clearly explained stating that after the petitioner was shifted to the hospital by the driver of the offending vehicle and complainant, the driver of the offending vehicle given assurance to meet the medical expenses.

After taking x-ray when it was found that petitioner has sustained fracture injury and when the complainant called the driver to his mobile phone he did not pick the call and he has not met the medical expenses, hence finally they lodged the complaint.

It is relevant to state here that though there is delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint, but if MLC as per Ex.P24 is perused, on the date of accident itself without any delay, the petitioner was shifted to Rajarajeshwarai Medical and College Hospital and given treatment to the petitioner on the history of RTA while going on two wheeler as pillion rider hit by four wheeler on 15-09-2024 around 1-15 pm.
The accident in question has occurred on the said date at 01-15 pm., and petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 15-09-2024 at 01-24 pm.,
Hence without any delay petitioner was shifted to the hospital.
Hence, the reason assigned by the petitioner for delay in lodging the complaint appears to be genuine and acceptable one.

15. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the spot mahazar is perused, the petitioner as pillion rider was proceeding towards Hejjala in Bangalore- Mysore road and offending vehicle came from Kumbalagodu side towards Bangalore dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner in which petitioner was the pillion rider and her husband was the rider.
The width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 40 feet and the accident in question has occurred at a distance of nearly 10 feet towards the right side.
It is one way road.

It clearly reveals that the offending vehicle came from wrong direction hit to the motorcycle that too by taking his vehicle on Monamma vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32640726/
4 the extreme right side of his road and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Though the respondent no.1 has disputed the manner of accident but they have not stated and proved the way in which according to them the accident in question has occurred.
The respondents have not examined the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further the respondent no.2 has remained ex-parte.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves that rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are at Ex.P.7 and Ex.P9.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 15-09- 2024 to 23-09-2024 at Rajarajeswari Medical College & Hospital for a period of 9 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury no.1 is simple in nature and injury no.2 is grievous in nature.
17. Dr.B Ramesh - Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, is examined as Pw-2 and through him OPD card and X-ray film are got marked as Ex.P19 and Ex.P20.
P.W.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 02-03-2025 for disability assessment.

PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has sustained permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 30% and whole body disability at 15% and that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.

18. The learned counsel for the petitioner at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in (2011) 13 SCC 323 between Nagarajappa Vs., Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.,
In the said case, the claimant who is coolie sustained injuries of compound fracture of ulnar styloid process of the left hand and subluxation of the left wrist.

entities.text: Nagarajappa Vs., Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctor assessed disability at 23% of whole body.
But the Tribunal assessed it as at 20%.
The findings of the Tribunal was affirmed by the Hon'ble High Court.
In the said case, it was observed that "Effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured has to be quantified in terms of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent disability.
The doctor assessed permanent residual physical disability of the upper limb at 68% and 22-23% of the whole body.
The fact that the accident has left him with one useless hand will severely affect his ability to perform his work as a collie or any other manual work.
The appellant is severally hampered and perhaps forever handicapped from performing his occupation as a coolie.

Thus, while computing loss of future income disability should be taken to be 68% and not 20%, as was done by the Tribunal and the High Court".
19.

In 2023 (20) SCC 774 between Mohd., Sabeer alias Shabir Hussain Vs. Regional Manager, U.P State Road Transport Corportion wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has considered the entire percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner to assessed the future loss of income and also added loss of future prospect.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel by referring aforesaid judgment has submitted that in the present case also the court has to consider the 30% of the disability and to add loss of future prospect.

sentences.text: If the judgment referred by the petitioner is read in whole wherein the petitioner has suffered an amputation of the lower right limb, crush injury on right leg, fracture tibia right leg and other injuries.
The doctor has assessed the disability at 70% however the Hon'ble High Court has considered the disability suffered by the petitioner at 35% so as to assess the future earing due to disability.
It is observed in the said case that the assessment of compensation for loss of future earnings would depend upon the impact and effect of the permanent disability on his earning capacity.
In the said case, the petitioner was scrap dealer and he was self employed and doctor has opinioned that the petitioner cannot to do his said work.
Under the given set of facts the Hon'ble Apex court has considered the disability at 70% and awarded compensation under the head loss of future prospects.
21. If the evidence of PW.2 is perused, he is not a treated doctor.
As per the own evidence of PW.2 the fracture is united and petitioner can do her daily work and supervision work with some difficulty.
It is nowhere stated stated by the PW.2 that petitioner cannot continue her work because of the disability suffered by her.
Hence, the observation made in the aforesaid judgment cannot be made applicable to the case in hand.
The PW2 having assessed the disability on right lower limb at 30% assessed the disability on whole body at 15%.

In the judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk it was observed that "normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3 rd of the particular limb".

2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this court inclines to consider the disability of petitioner at 10%.

22. Mr. Dhananjaya Kumar G V - Medical Record office Assistant at Rajarajeshwari Hospital,
Bangalore is examined as PW.3 and through him case sheet, x-ray film and MLC extract are got marked as Ex.P22 to Ex.P24.
23. Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
24. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
25. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, she has produced 17 medical bills for Rs.42,287/- as per Ex.P17.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.42,287/-.
26.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 31 years and she was working as coolie and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention, petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
27.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and taken treatment for 9 days as inpatient in Rajarajeswari Medical College & Hospital.

Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner Monamma vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32640726/
6 which is grievous in nature, it is reasonable to hold that period of four months as complete laid down period.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for 4 months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.66,000/- (16500X4)
towards loss of income during the laid down period.
28. From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Rajarajeswari Medical College & Hospital.
Further for 9 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
29. The petitioner has contended that she is aged about 31 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P11/Aadhar card which shows her date of birth as 01-01-1993 that means she was aged about 31 years.
Hence considering the Aadhaar card this Court has taken the age of the petitioner as 31 years.

30. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and by considering the evidence of PW.2 as he has assessed the disability on higher side this Court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 10% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 31 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 is '16'.
So by applying the multiplier '16' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.3,16,800/- (i.e., Rs.16,500 x 10% x 16 x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,16,800/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
31. So far as the future medical expenses is concerned, even though PW.2 has deposed that petitioner needs surgery in future for removal of implants, but he has not given any estimation.

Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.
32.
The petitioner at her age of 31 years has suffered grievous injury.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:

 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 66,000/-
 laid up period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  5.

 6. Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-

Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,80,087/- (Rupees Five Lakh Eighty Thousand Eighty Seven only).

sentences.text: 33. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
34. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,80,087/- + cost of Rs.750/- imposed vide order on IA No.III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.5,80,837/- (Rupees Five Lakh Eighty Thousand Eight Hundred Thirty Seven only).

After deducting cost of Rs.750/- and future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/- balance sum of Rs.5,50,087/-shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 60% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 40% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 3rd day of September 2025.)
